description: Machine-readable graft-material knowledge for OsteoQuant. Every numeric value carries an evidence tag; 'assumption' means not sourced and must be replaced by measurement. References are keys into docs/science/references.bib.

conventions.host_bone_reference_note: advisor convention; desktop micro-CT human trabecular bone TMD 940-1030 and SRmicroCT ~1150 (kazakia2008)
conventions.effective_energy_note: lab scans at 40-70 kVp with filtration are represented by 30-50 keV monoenergetic calculations [assumption]
conventions.advisor_profile_note: 'metal' is used for magnesium and titanium because osteoquant/advisor/separability.py refuses graft endpoints only when morphology == 'metal'

materials.name: Hydroxyapatite (sintered, synthetic)

typical_porosity.note: sub-voxel microporosity of sintered granules; designed macroporosity 100-500 um is usually resolved

ha_equivalent_mgHA_cm3.derivation: HA-equivalent of the dense solid phase computed from NIST XCOM elemental mass attenuation coefficients (mixture rule) at monoenergetic 30/40/50 keV, mapped to a bone model of HA in a soft-tissue matrix (osteoquant/phantom/materials.py; calculation script not shipped). Effective energy 30-50 keV is taken as representative of a filtered 40-70 kVp lab scan [assumption]. Apparent value of a porous granule = dense value x (1 - sub-voxel porosity) [physics; linear mixing with fluid]. Porosity 0.2-0.5 [assumption].

resorption.mechanism: very slow dissolution and cell-mediated resorption; osteoconductive surface

timelines.statement: pure HA implants often remain in the body for several years
about 10% of HA resorbed at 12 months vs 60% of beta-TCP
filler 34.5% at 2 wk, 31.2% at 8 wk

separability_intensity_only.reasoning: Dense or moderately porous sintered HA reads well above mature bone (dense 3154 mgHA/cm3 equivalent, ~2.9x host). Degrades to 'partial' for nanocrystalline/highly microporous HA, thin struts (<3 voxels) and the partial-volume rim at every granule surface, which takes bone-like values.
conditions_for_good: partial-volume rim handled (erosion band or edge model)

recommended_measurement_strategy: intensity threshold (calibrated) with partial-volume edge correction
texture/morphology model for porous or nanocrystalline HA
day-0 registration to quantify residual graft over time

supportable: new bone volume outside graft (with edge correction)
not_supportable_without_extra_evidence: bone-to-graft contact at voxel > 1/4 granule size
new bone volume for nanocrystalline/highly porous HA (histology calibration required)

materials.evidence_level: published + derived-physics; porosity and granule size are assumptions

advisor_profile.source: dense HA 3.155 g/cm3 -> 3154 mgHA/cm3 at 40 keV (NIST), x(1-0.30 microporosity) / 1075

materials.name: beta-Tricalcium phosphate

typical_porosity.note: grain size and porosity strongly modified by trace beta-CPP or HA impurities

Falls further as resorption thins and fragments granules.

resorption.mechanism: cell-mediated (osteoclastic) resorption plus dissolution; osteoconductive and osteoinductive

60% resorbed at 12 months (vs 10% HA)
CaP replacement by bone may take 3-36 months depending on age, site and metabolism

resorption.evidence: published; timelines differ by model by an order of magnitude

separability_intensity_only.reasoning: Intact granules at early timepoints are brighter than bone (dense 3024 mgHA/cm3 eq). As resorption proceeds the granules become microporous and fragmented and their apparent density enters the bone range; new bone is deposited directly on granule surfaces. Intensity alone is good at day 0-2 wk and degrades with time.

recommended_measurement_strategy: intensity threshold only at early timepoints with a measured material reference
texture/morphology model calibrated against histology for mid/late timepoints

supportable: residual graft volume at early timepoints (<= ~4 wk) when bimodal histogram confirmed
not_supportable_without_extra_evidence: new bone vs residual TCP at mid/late timepoints by intensity alone

advisor_profile.source: dense beta-TCP 3.067 g/cm3 -> 3024 mgHA/cm3 at 40 keV (NIST), x(1-0.50) / 1075; drops as it resorbs

materials.name: Calcium sulfate (hemihydrate set to dihydrate)

typical_porosity.note: melt-derived particulate is essentially dense; sol-gel glasses and scaffolds are porous

materials.name: Deproteinised bovine bone mineral (xenograft)

composition.formula: carbonated apatite of bovine bone with organic phase removed; sintered variants (e.g. cerabone, 1250 C) are more crystalline

theoretical_density_g_cm3.note: strut mineral packing as source bone tissue [inference]

ha_equivalent_mgHA_cm3.derivation: Struts retain the mineral of the source bone tissue at native packing, so the strut HA-equivalent is expected near bone tissue TMD (desktop micro-CT 940-1030, SRmicroCT/ash 1150-1300 for human trabecular bone; kazakia2008). Inference, not a measurement.

materials.name: Demineralised bone matrix

composition.formula: acid-extracted allograft matrix: collagens, non-collagenous proteins, growth factors, 1-6% residual calcium phosphate mineral; often in carriers (glycerol, hyaluronate, CMC, poloxamer, gelatin, collagen, calcium sulfate)

typical_granule_size_um.note: particles <250 um reported less osteoinductive than 420-840 um

ha_equivalent_mgHA_cm3.derivation: 1-6% residual mineral (gruskin2012) gives at most tens of mgHA/cm3; carriers such as calcium sulfate add their own attenuation

resorption.mechanism: matrix degradation releases growth factors; osteoinduction varies by lot and donor

separability_intensity_only.reasoning: Near-radiolucent at implantation (counts as soft tissue), so early mineral can be attributed to new bone; but DBM particles that remineralise or are incorporated into new bone are indistinguishable from it. Carrier minerals (e.g. CaSO4) break the radiolucent assumption.

recommended_measurement_strategy: report 'mineral in defect' rather than 'new bone'

supportable: total mineralised volume in defect (attributable to new bone only if carrier is non-mineral and stated as an assumption)

materials.name: Absorbable collagen sponge (incl. rhBMP-2 carrier)

unsupported_material_workflow.trigger: material id not in this file, or material present but advisor_profile.evidence is ASSUMPTION for the requested endpoint

steps.name: identify
steps.action: Record product name, lot, composition (supplier data sheet), form (granule/block/paste/strut), granule size, and whether it is bone-derived or contains a mineral carrier.

steps.name: characterise
steps.action: Scan the material alone (ex vivo, in the same medium as specimens, e.g. saline or the embedding resin) and a day-0 implanted defect with the SAME protocol (kVp, filter, voxel size, reconstruction, beam-hardening correction) and an HA calibration phantom.

steps.name: measure_intensity
steps.action: Convert to mgHA/cm3; compute the material intensity distribution after eroding 2 voxels from every surface (to exclude partial-volume rims); record mean, SD, percentiles and the rim distribution separately.

steps.name: reference_bone
steps.action: Measure host bone and, where available, new bone at the study's timepoints (or use a labelled pilot specimen) on the same calibrated scale.

steps.name: compute_separability
steps.action: Estimate the overlap of graft vs new-bone intensity distributions (e.g. Bayes error / Dice-optimal threshold), including partial-volume rims at the study voxel size; repeat for morphology features if a texture model is proposed.

steps.name: decide
steps.action: If intensity overlap is below the acceptance limit -> intensity threshold allowed (report threshold and overlap). If not -> require day-0 registration or a texture model validated on labelled scans (histology-registered or expert-annotated) from this material. If neither is available -> ABSTAIN: report only total mineralised volume and state that new-bone vs graft is not measurable.

steps.name: record
steps.action: Store the characterisation (scans, SHA-256, protocol, measured distributions, decision) as a new entry with evidence 'measured' and link it to the study audit log; re-characterise when the protocol or lot changes.

abstention_rules: never report new bone volume for a bone-derived graft (autograft, allograft, DBBM, remineralised DBM) from intensity alone
never transfer a threshold across kVp/filter for energy-dependent materials (glasses, calcium sulfate, Mg)
never report bone-to-graft contact when voxel size > 1/4 of the granule size
